narrative.northStar: A private archive with four distinct visual worlds
narrative.overview: NaviHUB presents a local media library and learning workspace through shared semantic surfaces. Lain's Wired, after dark palette uses black violet and rose terminal signals; Solid / Ink pairs paper and dark green ink with red actions. Lain remains the default. Home keeps the user's own mixed-media cover wall, a theme-specific text scrim and selected local theme art, and a real resume destination ahead of configurable widgets. Solid / Ink uses red-filled active navigation; Lain uses a signal-tinted surface with a leading edge. Hatsune Miku adds the approved cyan-filled option two with Quicksand and RITAO artwork; Twin Peaks adds warm curtain red, ivory, Bodoni Moda and classic/FWWM imagery. Neither inherits Lain atmosphere.
keyCharacteristics: Shared semantic surface, ink, line and signal roles across all four palettes
Compact desktop navigation with geometry specific to each selected theme
Theme-specific typography and locally bundled identity artwork
Quiet study surfaces and explicit high-contrast media islands
Theme-specific section bars and navigation active states

rules.name: The Semantic Surface Rule
rules.body: Use shared semantic surface, ink, line, and signal roles for application chrome; reserve explicit contrast islands for readers and overlays on art.

rules.name: The Signal Meaning Rule
rules.body: Keep action/live, link, anomaly, affirmative, and caution signals semantically distinct in all themes.

rules.name: The Resume First Rule
rules.body: Home keeps its pinned cover wall and selected art, then presents a real resume or in-progress destination before configurable widgets.

dos: Use semantic theme roles for shared application chrome.
Keep study routes readable, quiet, and keyboard focused.
Preserve the user's selected theme assets and local font stacks.
donts: Do not turn the pinned Home cover wall into a configurable widget.
Do not carry Lain glow or scanlines into Solid / Ink or quiet study routes.
Do not weaken contrast over artwork or add decorative glyphs.
